CV

Yung Hsing (Winston) Huang

Research Scientist / Bioinformatician

Houston, TX | (832) 664-1350 | winstonhyh@live.com
Lawful Permanent Resident (USA) | Canadian Citizen

Summary

  • 8 years of academic and industrial research experience; 3 years in bioinformatics.
  • Expertise: RNA editing, epigenetics, spatial transcriptomics (Xenium), single-cell multi-omics, gene signature development.

Work Experience

Senior Staff Scientist — Baylor College of Medicine | Houston, TX | 07/2026–Present

Shared bioinformatics scientist between labs of Dr. Bruno Di Stefano and Dr. Margaret Goodell.

  • Leveraging SLURM cloud computing for end-to-end multi-omics pipelines (RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, WGBS, EM-seq, RNA editing seq).
  • Building AI/ML models to predict the RNA editome from bulk RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data.
  • Investigating how P-bodies, RNA-binding proteins, and transposable elements reprogram cell fate as opportunities for cancer therapy.
  • Studying clonal hematopoiesis contributions to hematological malignancies.

Bioinformatician — Houston Methodist Research Institute | Houston, TX | 02/2024–07/2026

Spatial Omics Core and Chan Lab

  • Integrating Xenium spatial transcriptomics with single-cell T-cell repertoire sequencing from a phase II clinical trial (manuscript in preparation).
  • Architected SLURM-based workflows to process large-scale Xenium datasets (>10⁶ cells).
  • Developed HMRIBladdeR, an R/Shiny app for gene/signature prognostic assessment in public bladder cancer cohorts.
  • Analyzed single-cell RNA-seq and Xenium spatial data to characterize CAF heterogeneity in non-muscle-invasive vs. muscle-invasive bladder cancer (Gao et al., Sci Adv, 2025; manuscript in preparation).
  • Developed a Caspase-1-driven pyroptosis gene signature using Cox models and visualized the intratumoral pyroptotic niche via Xenium spatial transcriptomics (Wong et al., Nat Commun, 2026).
  • Characterized therapy-induced senescent tumor cell niches and ligand-receptor interactions in minimal residual disease using Xenium data (Liu et al., Nat Commun, under revision).
  • Received Exceptional Employee Bonus in 2025 and 2026 (top 10% performers at Houston Methodist Hospital).
  • Mentoring two PhD students on bioinformatics aspects of their projects.

Bioengineer — Systemic Bio (3D Systems) | Houston, TX | 06/2022–11/2023

  • Designed experimental workflows generating high-content data (viability, proteomics, transcriptomics) for organ-on-chip drug screening.
  • Built standardized analysis pipelines to process and visualize multi-modal assay data for drug efficacy/toxicity profiling.
  • Partnered with major pharma stakeholders on million-scale funded projects; translated complex outputs into actionable preclinical insights.
  • Evaluated biomaterial biocompatibility using IHC/qPCR, bridging material science and biological validation.

Postdoctoral Fellow — Houston Methodist Research Institute | Houston, TX | 04/2019–05/2022

  • Identified NHE6 as a therapeutic target to improve therapy efficacy in resistant multiple myeloma (Huang et al., Drug Res Updates, 2026).
  • Wrote and generated preliminary data for a funded CPRIT grant: “Targeting NHE6 to improve clinical efficacy of daratumumab in myeloma” (RP220639).

    Practicum: In silico drug screening for KMT2A::AFF1 fusion protein (Huang et al., iScience, 2026).

Patent

Core Skills

  • NGS Analyses: bulk RNA-seq, scRNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics (Xenium), TCR-seq, ribo-seq, ATAC-seq, WGBS/EM-seq.
  • Bioinformatics: Gene signature development, in silico drug screening/docking, public dataset mining (TCGA, GEO, EMBL-EBI).
